(1) the diagnostic decisions of physicians are often suboptimal, (2) the diagnostic decisions made by physicians are not improved by the use of diagnostic aids, (3) the diagnostic decisions are improved by the use of a computerized decision aid, (4) the diagnostic decisions improved by the computerized decision aid are not further improved by the addition of the diagnostic aids, and (5) the computerized decision support system is not improved by the addition of the diagnostic aids.
the use of diagnostic tests in medical and legal settings can be greatly improved through the use of a simple and powerful decision-making method called the “receiver-operating characteristic” (ROC).
